definitions.explanation: A tall grass that grows in wetlands, along rivers, and in marshy areas. Used historically for thatching, mat-making, and as a literary symbol.

examples.japanese: {川辺|かわべ}に{葦|あし}が{茂|しげ}っている。
examples.english: Reeds are growing thick along the riverbank.

examples.japanese: {風|かぜ}が{吹|ふ}くと{葦|あし}が{一斉|いっせい}に{揺|ゆ}れた。
examples.english: When the wind blew, the reeds all swayed together.

examples.japanese: パスカルは「{人間|にんげん}は{考|かんが}える{葦|あし}である」という{有名|ゆうめい}な{言葉|ことば}を{残|のこ}した。
examples.english: Pascal left the famous words, 'Man is a thinking reed.'

notes:
Also read as よし. The alternate reading よし arose because あし sounds like {悪|あ}し (bad), so the euphemistic reading よし ({良|よ}し, good) was adopted. Both readings are correct.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {葦|あし}が{茂|しげ}る (reeds grow thick)
- {葦原|あしはら} (reed field, reed bed)
- {葦|あし}の{葉|は} (reed leaves)
- {葦簀|よしず} (reed screen/blind — note: usually read よしず)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The phrase {考|かんが}える{葦|あし} (thinking reed) from Pascal's Pensées is widely known in Japan. {葦原|あしはら} also appears in classical texts as part of {葦原|あしはら}の{中|なか}つ{国|くに}, an ancient name for Japan.
